mutations.before:
const baselinePairs = new Set(pairsOf(baseline).map((f) => `${f.above}->${f.below}`));
  return pairsOf(layers).filter((f) => !baselinePairs.has(`${f.above}->${f.below}`));
mutations.because: The absolute scan, which is what this function looked like in its first cut and what a reader reaches for: 'every occluding pair the stack contains'. It is wrong on exactly the template every campaign uses. `image-text` is [image, shade, accent, static-text, logo] and `logo` obscures `static-text` by the table, so the mutant reports an advisory on every default creative ever rendered — on a pair `drawLogo` actively resolves by snapping to an inset edge — and writes an `occlusionAdvisories` key onto every asset, moving the report bytes of every brief that never touched its layers. Caught by the canonical-introduces-nothing property, which is the whole reason the baseline is a parameter.
command: the canonical stack introduces nothing over itself
